record.title: The generating-level conjecture for the linear free divisors of type D_n
record.statement:
Let $D\subset X=\mathbb{C}^{4n-10}$ be the linear free divisor $D_n$. The Hodge filtration on $\mathcal{O}_X(*D)$ is **generated at level** $k$ when

$$
F_l\mathcal{D}_X\cdot F_k\mathcal{O}_X(*D)=F_{k+l}\mathcal{O}_X(*D)
$$

for every $l\geq 0$. **Generating-level conjecture for $D_n$.** The Hodge filtration on $\mathcal{O}_X(*D)$ is generated at level $n-3$. This estimate is presented as a consequence that would follow from the paper's general generating-level conjecture, and extends the observed calculations for the $D_n$ series. It remains open insofar as the parent conjecture is unproved.
record.source_name: Alberto Castaño Domínguez, Luis Narváez Macarro and Christian Sevenheck, “Hodge ideals of free divisors”, arXiv:1912.09786 (2022).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.09786

record.title: Bipartite DRR classification conjecture for finite groups
record.statement: Let $R$ be a finite group with a subgroup $M$ of index $2$. A **bipartite DRR** is a Cayley graph $\operatorname{Cay}(R,S)$, with $S\subseteq R\setminus M$, whose automorphism group is the regular representation of $R$. **Bipartite DRR classification conjecture.** One of the following holds: $(R,M)$ admits a bipartite DRR, or $R$ is one of the $22$ groups listed in Table 1. Thus, apart from the stated exceptional groups, every finite group with an index-$2$ subgroup admits a subset $S\subseteq R\setminus M$ producing a bipartite DRR.
record.source_name: Jia-Li Du, Yan-Quan Feng and Pablo Spiga, “A conjecture on bipartite graphical regular representations”, arXiv:2001.03918 (2020).

record.title: Finite-n peak at four missing differences
record.statement:
Let $P_n^{\mathrm{M}}(k)$ denote the probability that a uniformly random subset $S\subseteq[n]$ has exactly $k$ missing differences, namely

$$
P_n^{\mathrm{M}}(k)=\Pr\bigl(2n-1-|S-S|=k\bigr).
$$

**Peak-at-four conjecture.** For all $n\ge 15$ and every $k\ne4$,

$$
P_n^{\mathrm{M}}(4)>P_n^{\mathrm{M}}(k).
$$

The paper proves that the limiting value at $k=4$ is larger than the other values, and experimental data suggest that $n=15$ already suffices; the conjecture supplies this explicit finite threshold.
record.source_name: Scott Harvey-Arnold, Steven J. Miller and Fei Peng, “Distribution of missing differences in diffsets”, arXiv:2001.08931 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.08931

record.title: The first negative eigenvalue conjecture for Siegel Hecke eigenforms
record.statement:
Let $F$ be an arbitrary Siegel Hecke eigenform of degree $2$ and weight $k\geq 20$, with Hecke eigenvalues $\lambda_F(n)$ and analytic conductor $Q_F$. For $\epsilon>0$, write $n$ for the least positive integer such that $\lambda_F(n)<0$.

**First negative eigenvalue conjecture.** For every $\epsilon>0$, one has

$$
n\ll_{\epsilon} Q_F^{1/2+\epsilon},
$$

where the implied constant is absolute apart from its dependence on $\epsilon$.

The paper proves a stronger bound for Yoshida lifts under a condition on the conductors of the underlying forms. This conjecture proposes the analogous convexity-scale bound for arbitrary degree-two Siegel Hecke eigenforms, and the source suggests that an exponent strictly smaller than $1/2$ might also be possible.
record.source_name: Soumya Das and Ritwik Pal, “The first negative eigenvalue of Yoshida lifts”, arXiv:2002.00546 (2020).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.00546

record.title: The Atkin–Lehner equidistribution conjecture for level-2 modular forms
record.statement:
Let $k\geq 2$, and let $S_k(\Gamma_0(2))$ be the space of cusp forms of weight $k$ and level $2$. Let $W_2$ denote the Atkin–Lehner operator, and set

$$
d=\dim_\mathbb{C}S_k(\Gamma_0(2)).
$$

**Atkin–Lehner equidistribution conjecture.** For all $k\geq 2$, the space $S_k(\Gamma_0(2))$ decomposes under $W_2$ into Hecke-irreducible subspaces of dimensions $\lfloor d/2\rfloor$ and $\lceil d/2\rceil$.

This is an analogue of the Maeda conjecture for level $2$, predicting that the Hecke-irreducible pieces in the two Atkin–Lehner eigenspaces are as evenly sized as possible. The source reports computational evidence through weight $400$, while the assertion is not established in general.
record.source_name: Alex J. Best, Jonathan Bober, Andrew R. Booker, Edgar Costa, John Cremona, Maarten Derickx, Min Lee, David Lowry-Duda, David Roe, Andrew V. Sutherland and John Voight, “Computing classical modular forms”, arXiv:2002.04717 (2022).

record.title: Monotonicity of Robin's inequality under increasing prime exponents
record.statement: Let $n= p_1^{k_1}p_2^{k_2}\dots p_m^{k_m}>5040$, where the $p_i$ are distinct primes and the $k_i$ are positive integers. For an index $j$, form the integer $n'=p_1^{k_1}p_2^{k_2}\dots p_j^{k_j+1}\ldots p_m^{k_m}$ by increasing the exponent of $p_j$ by one. **Prime-exponent extension conjecture.** The resulting integer $n'$ is also valid for all values of $j$, i.e. it satisfies Robin's inequality whenever $n$ does. This conjecture would provide the final step toward extending Robin's inequality from the single-power prime products considered in the preceding conjecture to all integers $n>5040$; the source presents it as an unproved further conjecture.

record.title: Burstein–Jones Wilf-equivalence conjecture for Dumont-1 permutations
record.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{D}^1_{2n}$ denote the set of Dumont-1 permutations of length $2n$, and let $\mathfrak{D}^1_{2n}(\tau)$ denote those avoiding the pattern $\tau$. **Burstein–Jones's Wilf-equivalence conjecture.** For all $n\geq 0$,

$$
|\mathfrak{D}^1_{2n}(2143)|=|\mathfrak{D}^1_{2n}(3421)|.
$$

The conjecture asserts that the two avoidance sequences are equal for every $n$. They agree computationally through $n=10$, but the source says that the conjecture is difficult to prove and only partial progress was known.

record.title: Weak extremal comparison conjecture for increasing and final-descent patterns
record.statement:
Let $m\geq3$ and $r\geq1$. **Weak extremal comparison conjecture.** There exists $n_0\in\mathbb{N}$ such that for every natural number $n>n_0$,

$$
|\operatorname{Av}_{n}(\operatorname{dist}_{r}(12\cdots m))|\geq|\operatorname{Av}_{n}(\operatorname{dist}_{r}(12\cdots(m-2)m(m-1)))|.
$$

This is a weaker version of the two preceding extremal conjectures and asks only for the comparison between the increasing pattern and the pattern obtained by swapping the final two letters. The source says that a suitable injection establishing this inequality is desired; no resolution is reported.
record.source_name: Stoyan Dimitrov, “On permutation patterns with constrained gap sizes”, arXiv:2002.12322 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.12322

record.title: Revstack fertility monotonicity conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\operatorname{revstack}=s\circ\operatorname{rev}$, where $s$ is the stack-sorting map and $\operatorname{rev}$ reverses a permutation. For a permutation $\sigma\in S_n$, let $\operatorname{revstack}^{-1}(\sigma)$ denote its set of preimages under $\operatorname{revstack}$. **Revstack fertility monotonicity conjecture.** For every permutation $\sigma\in S_n$,

$$
|\operatorname{revstack}^{-1}(\sigma)|\leq|\operatorname{revstack}^{-1}(\operatorname{revstack}(\sigma))|,
$$

with equality if and only if $\sigma=123\cdots n$. The source presents this as an open conjecture related to fertility monotonicity.
record.source_name: Colin Defant, “Fertility Monotonicity and Average Complexity of the Stack-Sorting Map”, arXiv:2003.05935 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.05935

record.title: The 4/4 conjecture for permutation rational functions
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field, and let $N_{v,u}(q)$ denote the number of permutation rational functions $V(x)/U(x)$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ with numerator degree $v$ and denominator degree $u$. **The 4/4 conjecture.** For all prime powers $q$, 

$$
N_{4,4}(q)=\frac{(q+1)q^2(q-1)^3}{3}.
$$

The formula has been verified computationally for all primes $p\leq 47$ and concerns permutation rational functions of equal numerator and denominator degree.
record.source_name: Sergey Bereg, Brian Malouf, Linda Morales, Thomas Stanley and I. Hal Sudborough, “Improved Lower Bounds for Permutation Arrays Using Permutation Rational Functions”, arXiv:2003.10072 (2021).

record.title: A prime-representing quadratic-exponent conjecture following Mills
record.statement:
Let $f(n)=\lfloor A^{(n+1)^2}\rfloor$ for a positive constant $A$.

**Prime-representing function conjecture.** There is a constant $A$, possibly near $1.1966746500705764022$, such that $f(n)$ is prime for every integer $n\geq 1$.

This conjecture proposes a deterministic prime-representing function with quadratic exponents, analogous to Mills' formula. The stated value of $A$ is experimental, and the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Christian Elsholtz, “Unconditional Prime-representing Functions, Following Mills”, arXiv:2004.01285 (2020).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.01285

record.title: Per Alexandersson's MNability conjecture for Petrie functions times $p_2$
record.statement:
Let $G(k,m)\in\Lambda$ be the Petrie symmetric function, let $p_2$ be the second power-sum symmetric function, let $\operatorname{Par}$ denote the set of partitions, and let $s_\lambda$ denote the Schur function indexed by $\lambda$. **Alexandersson's MNability conjecture.** For every positive integer $k$ and every $n\in\mathbb{N}$, $G(k,m)\cdot p_2$ can be written as

$$
\sumnonlimits\limits_{\lambda\in\operatorname{Par}}u_\lambda s_\lambda
$$

with $u_\lambda\in\{-1,0,1\}$ for all $\lambda\in\operatorname{Par}$. The conjecture has been verified for all $k$ and $n$ satisfying $k+n\leq 30$, but the statement contains an apparent parameter mismatch, using $n$ in the quantifier and $m$ in $G(k,m)$; this should be checked against the source.
record.source_name: Darij Grinberg, “Petrie symmetric functions”, arXiv:2004.11194 (2021).

record.title: Conjectured recurrences for five lexicographically least pattern-avoiding words
record.statement:
Let $d4e6_{a/b}$ denote the lexicographically least infinite word on the nonnegative integers avoiding $p/q$-powers for $p/q\geq a/b$, and write $w(i)$ for the letter at position $i$ of the relevant word. **Conjecture on five unknown words.** For all $i\geq 0$, the letters satisfy

$$
w(41190i+41201)=w(i)+3
$$

for $d4e6_{7/6}$,

$$
w(340i+52670)=w(i)+3
$$

for $d4e6_{8/7}$,

$$
w(44i+2701)=w(i)+2
$$

for $d4e6_{9/7}$,

$$
w(26i+428)=w(i)+\begin{cases}0&\text{if }i=0,\\1&\text{if }i\neq0,\end{cases}
$$

for $d4e6_{10/7}$, and

$$
w(22763i+22850)=w(i)+2
$$

for $d4e6_{15/8}$. These words are among the simplest whose structures were not known. The paper notes that no conjecture was available for $d4e6_{11/6}$ or $d4e6_{11/8}$, and that the general proof strategy remains unavailable.
record.source_name: Eric Rowland and Manon Stipulanti, “Avoiding 5/4-powers on the alphabet of nonnegative integers”, arXiv:2005.03158 (2020).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.03158

record.title: Parity-unimodality conjecture for fake-degree polynomials
record.statement:
For a partition $clambda$, let $f^{clambda}(q)$ be its fake-degree polynomial. A polynomial with coefficients $a_0,a_1,a_2,cdots$ is **parity-unimodal** when the even-indexed coefficient sequence $a_0,a_2,a_4,cdots$ and the odd-indexed coefficient sequence $a_1,a_3,a_5,cdots$ are each unimodal.

**Parity-unimodality conjecture.** The fake-degree polynomials $f^{clambda}(q)$ are parity-unimodal for all partitions $clambda$.

The conjecture is motivated by results on $q$-Catalan polynomials and computational checks for $n\leq 50$. Its resolution is not indicated in the supplied text.

record.title: The degree conjecture for the associated Boolean function of odd-variable APN functions
record.statement:
Let $F$ be a quadratic APN function of $n$ variables, where $n$ is odd, and let $\varphi_F:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{F}_2$ be the associated Boolean function in the representation of $\gamma_F$.

**Degree conjecture.** Then

$$
\deg(\varphi_F)<n,
$$

or, equivalently, $\operatorname{wt}(\varphi_F)$ is even.

The case of odd $n$ is stated to remain open. The conjecture is supported by computational experiments for all known quadratic APN functions in at most 11 variables.
record.source_name: Anastasiya Gorodilova, “A note on the properties of associated Boolean functions of quadratic APN functions”, arXiv:2005.10788 (2020).

record.title: Converse CDE conjecture for ordinary Young diagrams
record.statement:
Let $\lambda$ be a Young diagram. The interval $[\emptyset,\lambda]$ is the lower interval in Young's lattice, and the CDE property is the coincidence of the expected down-degree and up-degree statistics with the corresponding rank-uniform averages. A Young diagram is **balanced** when the left cell of every inner corner lies on the line joining the top right corner of the last cell in its first row to the bottom left corner of the last cell in its first column; the slope may be any value.

**Converse CDE conjecture.** The interval $[\emptyset,\lambda]$ has the CDE property if and only if $\lambda$ is balanced.

The forward implication for balanced diagrams is known, while the converse was checked for all partitions of size at most $30$ and remains open in general.
record.source_name: Jang Soo Kim, Michael J. Schlosser and Meesue Yoo, “Enumeration of standard barely set-valued tableaux of shifted shapes”, arXiv:2006.03253 (2020).

record.title: The Lin–Ma conjecture on 0012-avoiding inversion sequences
record.statement:
An **inversion sequence** of length $n$ is a sequence $e=e_1e_2\cdots e_n$ such that $0\le e_i\le i-1$ for $1\le i\le n$; let $\mathbf{I}_n(0012)$ denote the set of inversion sequences of length $n$ avoiding the pattern $0012$. **Lin–Ma conjecture.** For every $n\ge 1$, 

$$
|\mathbf{I}_n(0012)|=1+\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}\binom{2i}{i-1}.
$$

This conjecture concerns the enumeration of inversion sequences avoiding a fixed pattern. The paper's abstract says that the authors confirm the conjecture and also obtain a formula for the subclass in which the last entry equals $n-1$, so the conjecture is solved.
record.source_name: Shane Chern, “On 0012-avoiding inversion sequences and a Conjecture of Lin and Ma”, arXiv:2006.04318 (2020).

record.title: The list-recoloring conjecture for planar graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph on $n$ vertices, let $L$ be a list assignment for $G$, and let 
$$
and $'$ be $L$-colorings of $G$. A proper $L$-coloring assigns to each vertex a color from its list, with adjacent vertices receiving different colors.

**List-recoloring conjecture.** If either

- $|L(v)|\ge 10$ for every $v\in V(G)$, or
- $G$ is triangle-free and $|L(v)|\ge 7$ for every $v\in V(G)$,

then
$$
 can be transformed to $'$ by $O(n)$ recolorings, with every intermediate coloring a proper $L$-coloring.

The paper notes that its ordinary-coloring theorems likely generalize to list coloring, but does not establish this statement. The claim would extend the linear-diameter recoloring results from fixed color sets to vertex-specific lists.

record.title: Path-cordiality characterization for finite abelian groups
record.statement: Let $A$ be a finite abelian group, and let $\mathbb{P}$ be the class of path graphs. A group is **$\mathbb{P}$-cordial** if every path graph is $A$-cordial, where $A$-cordiality means that the induced vertex-label and edge-label partitions are almost rectangular. **Path-cordiality conjecture.** The group $A$ is $\mathbb{P}$-cordial if and only if $A$ is not a nontrivial product of copies of $\mathbb{Z}_2$; equivalently, if and only if there exists $a\in A$ with $|a|>2$. The conjecture is verified for all finite abelian groups of order less than $24$, and its odd-order direction is proved, while the even-order case with an element of order greater than $2$ remains partially open.
record.source_name: Rebecca Patrias and Oliver Pechenik, “Path-cordial abelian groups”, arXiv:2006.13764 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.13764

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2020). “A major open problem is Hovey's conjecture that all trees are $A$-cordial for all cyclic groups $A$.”

record.title: Uniform Berry–Esseen conjecture for Rademacher sums
record.statement:
Let $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ be independent random variables uniformly distributed in $\{-1,1\}$, and let

$$
X=\sum_i a_i x_i
$$

be a Rademacher sum with $\operatorname{Var}(X)=1$ and $0<a_i\leq a_1$ for every $i$. Let $Z\sim N(0,1)$ be a standard Gaussian, and let $x\in\mathbb R$. **Berry–Esseen conjecture.**

$$
\left|\Pr[X\leq x]-\Pr[Z\leq x]\right|\leq \Pr[Z\in(0,a_1)]<\frac{a_1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}.
$$

This is proposed as a natural extension of a previously proved bound for coefficients bounded by $0.22$. The source presents it as an open problem, with no resolution supplied.
record.source_name: Nathan Keller and Ohad Klein, “Proof of Tomaszewski's Conjecture on Randomly Signed Sums”, arXiv:2006.16834 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.16834

record.title: Bound on zero-block lengths in the 2-adic expansion of zeta
record.statement:
Let $\zeta\in\mathbb{Z}_2$ be the $2$-adic number defined in Equation~, and let $\ell_\zeta(a)$ denote the length of the zero block beginning at the relevant digit position indexed by $a$. **Zero-block length conjecture.** For every $a\geq 0$,

$$
\ell_\zeta(a)\leq\frac{2}{95}a+\frac{18}{5}.
$$

By Proposition~, such a bound would control the growth rate of $\nu_2(U_i)$ through the approximability of $\zeta$ by non-negative integers. The source gives no proof or resolution of this assertion.

record.title: Hou–Jagadeesan convexity conjecture for partition ranks modulo 2
record.statement:
Let $N(r,2;n)$ denote the number of partitions of $n$ whose rank is congruent to $r$ modulo $2$, for $r\in\{0,1\}$. **Hou–Jagadeesan's conjecture.** If $r=0$ (respectively, $r=1$), then

$$
N(r,2;a)N(r,2;b)>N(r,2;a+b)
$$

for all $a,b\geq 11$ (respectively, $a,b\geq 12$). The paper states that this conjecture is proved by its main theorem, establishing the claimed convexity bound modulo $2$ after earlier work on the analogous modulus-$3$ result.

record.title: The stabilization-time conjecture for the map \operatorname{SC}_{231}
record.statement:
Let $n\geq 3$, let $S_n$ be the set of permutations of $[n]$, and let $\operatorname{Av}_n(132,231)$ denote the permutations avoiding $132$ and $231$.

**Stabilization-time conjecture.** For every $\pi\in S_n$,

$$
\operatorname{SC}_{231}^{2n-4}(\pi)\in\operatorname{Av}_n(132,231).
$$

Furthermore, there exists $\tau\in S_n$ such that

$$
\operatorname{SC}_{231}^{2n-5}(\tau)\notin\operatorname{Av}_n(132,231).
$$

The conjecture has been verified for $n\leq 9$ and predicts the sharp number of iterations needed to reach the periodic-point set for this map.

record.title: Conjecture comparing the elements $\xi_1(a,b)$ and Eisenstein motivic elements
record.statement:
For an integer $N\geq 1$ and $a,b\in\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$, let $\xi_1(a,b)$ and $\mathrm{Eis}^{0,0,1}(a,b)$ be the motivic elements introduced in the paper in $H^2_{\mathcal{M}}(X_1(N),\mathbb{Q}(3))$. **Comparison conjecture for $\xi_1(a,b)$.** For every integer $N\geq 1$ and every $a,b\in\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$, one has

$$
\xi_1(a,b)=\frac{N^2}{6}\mathrm{Eis}^{0,0,1}(a,b).
$$

The equality is motivated by regulator computations, which verify the corresponding numerical relation for every $N\leq 28$ to at least 40 decimal places. A modular proof is expected, but remains open in the supplied text.

record.title: Rank-symmetry conjecture for odd diagram classes
record.statement: Let $D$ be an odd diagram, and let $\operatorname{Perm}_n(D)$ denote its associated odd diagram class in Bruhat order. A subset of a graded poset is **rank-symmetric** when the number of elements at rank $r$ equals the number at the complementary rank for every $r$. **Rank-symmetry conjecture.** $\operatorname{Perm}_n(D)$ is rank-symmetric for any odd diagram $D$. This conjecture is motivated by computational evidence for $n\leq 10$; the source gives no proof or resolution, so the claim remains open.

record.title: Spectral formula conjecture for the matrix associated with a partition
record.statement:
Let $\nu$ be a partition of $N$ such that the associated polynomial $P^{[\nu]}$ has only simple roots, and let $J^{[\nu]}$ be the $N\times N$ matrix defined by the paper. Let $\rho^{[\nu]}=(\rho^{[\nu]}_1,\dots,\rho^{[\nu]}_N)$ be the rational sequence associated with $\nu$.

**Spectral formula conjecture.** The eigenvalues of $J^{[\nu]}$ are

$$
\lambda_k=2\bigl(\rho^{[\nu]}_k\bigr)^2,\qquad k=1,\dots,N,
$$

not necessarily distinct. Consequently,

$$
\det\bigl(J^{[\nu]}\bigr)=2^N\prod_{k=1}^N\bigl(\rho^{[\nu]}_k\bigr)^2,
$$

which is a strictly positive integer.

The formula was verified numerically for all non-degenerate partitions with $N\leq 10$. For the partition $\nu=(N)$, it specializes to the Hermite case, with eigenvalues $2,2\cdot4,\dots,2N^2$.
record.source_name: Riccardo Conti and Davide Masoero, “Counting monster potentials”, arXiv:2009.14638 (2020).

record.title: Existence conjecture for type 2 cyclic Legendre difference families
record.statement:
Let $(X,Y)$ be a Legendre difference family in the cyclic group ${\mathbb Z}_v$. It is of **type $2$** when neither block is a difference set; equivalently, if one block is a difference set then both are, and the family is of type $1$.

**Type 2 existence conjecture.** Legendre difference families of type $2$ exist for all odd lengths $v>8$.

This is presented as a stronger version of the conjecture that cyclic Legendre difference families exist for every odd length $v>2$. The constructions in the paper concern new lengths $91$, $93$, and $123$, while the asserted all-length type $2$ existence remains open.

record.title: Existence conjecture for nice Browkin continued fractions
record.statement: Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $\mathcal{Y}$ denote the set used in the paper for the allowed partial quotients, and let a **nice BCF** be a finite Browkin continued fraction satisfying the niceness conditions defined earlier in the paper. **Existence conjecture for nice BCFs.** For every integer $t\geq 1$, there exists a nice BCF of length $t$, except when $t=1$ and $p=3$. Nice sequences are the input to the paper's construction of infinitely many quadratic irrationals with periodic BCF expansions of period $2t$. The statement is marked resolved in the supplied status evidence: the exceptional $t=1$ case was proved in Bedocchi (1989).

record.title: Sankar's three-dimensional Catalan formula for reduced valid hook configurations
record.statement:
Let $\operatorname{RedVHC}_k(\operatorname{Av}_{3k-i}(312))$ denote the set of $312$-avoiding reduced valid hook configurations with $k$ hooks on permutations with $2k+i$ points. Define

$$
f_k(x)=\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}\left|\operatorname{RedVHC}_k(\operatorname{Av}_{3k-i}(312))\right|x^i,
$$

and let $h_k(x)=f_k(x-1)$. **Sankar's conjecture.** For all $k\geq 1$,

$$
f_k(0)=h_k(1)=\left|\operatorname{RedVHC}_k(\operatorname{Av}_{3k}(312))\right|=2\frac{(3k)!}{k!(k+1)!(k+2)!}.
$$

The right-hand side is the $k$th three-dimensional Catalan number; the source presents this as one of Sankar's conjectures about these counting polynomials, and the supplied material gives no resolution status.

record.title: Euclidean distance degree for diagonal-zero rank-two varieties
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{L}_2^S\subset\mathbb{C}^{m\times n}$ be the variety of matrices of rank at most $2$ with diagonal zero pattern $S=\{(1,1),\ldots,(s,s)\}$, where $s\in[4]$, and set $l=\min(m,n)$. **Diagonal-zero ED-degree conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{EDdegree}(\mathcal{L}_2^S)=
\begin{cases}
3(l-1)^2-2(l-1) & \text{if }s=1,\\
18(l-2)^2+6(l-2)+1 & \text{if }s=2\text{ and }m\ne n,\\
18(l-2)^2+10(l-2)+1 & \text{if }s=2\text{ and }m=n,\\
108(l-3)^2+144(l-3)+30 & \text{if }s=3\text{ and }m=n,\\
648(l-4)^2+1600(l-4)+488 & \text{if }s=4\text{ and }m=n.
\end{cases}
$$

These formulas are experimentally supported for the cases tabulated in the paper. The supplied text does not establish them in general, and the displayed cases do not specify formulas for every combination of $m,n,s$.

record.title: The sharp comparison conjecture for the triangular ratio and $w_{\mathbb{B}^2}$ metrics
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb{B}^2$ be the unit disk, and let $s_{\mathbb{B}^2}$ and $w_{\mathbb{B}^2}$ denote the triangular ratio metric and the function defined in the paper, respectively. **The sharp comparison conjecture for the triangular ratio and $w_{\mathbb{B}^2}$ metrics.** For all $x,y\in\mathbb{B}^2$, the inequality

$$
s_{\mathbb{B}^2}(x,y)\leq c\,w_{\mathbb{B}^2}(x,y)
$$

holds with the sharp constant

$$
c=\sqrt{\frac{h_0^2-2h_0+2}{2h_0^2-2\sqrt{2}h_0+2}}\approx1.07313,\qquad h_0=\frac{1-\sqrt{9-6\sqrt{2}}}{2-\sqrt{2}}.
$$

The inequality is supported by numerical tests beyond the special case proved earlier, and the stated sharp constant and its universal validity remain open.

record.title: Minimal-volume conjecture for exceptional-order fullerenes
record.statement:
Let $C_N$ be the class of fullerene isomers with $N$ atoms. Assume $N
eq 20,24,26,28,34$, $N
eq 10s$, and $N
eq 6k-4$, where $k\geq 5$ and $s\geq 2$. A nanotubical fullerene graph has a tubular part and two caps, with caps of types (c) and (d) among the possible cap types. **Minimal-volume conjecture for exceptional-order fullerenes.** If a fullerene isomer with number of atoms $N$ has the minimal hyperbolic volume in the class $C_N$, then it is a nanotubical fullerene graph with caps of type (c) or (d). Computations cited in the paper identify the relevant cap classes for all $N\leq 216$ subject to the stated exclusions, but the conjecture asserts the structural conclusion in general.

record.title: Quantum Laurent coefficient positivity conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\Delta$ be an ideal triangulation of $\frak{S}$ and let $\mathbb{I}^q_\Delta$ be the proposed quantum duality map. **Quantum Laurent coefficient positivity conjecture.** For every $\ell\in\mathscr{A}_{{\rm SL}_3,\frak{S}}(\mathbb{Z}^{T})$, the element $\mathbb{I}^q_\Delta(\ell)$ is a non-commutative Laurent polynomial in $\{\widehat{X}^{\pm1}_v\mid v\in\mathcal{V}(Q_\Delta)\}$ with coefficients in

$$
\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}[q^{\pm1/18}].
$$

This is the quantum analogue of Laurent coefficient positivity, with emphasis on non-negative coefficients; the source gives no resolution.

record.title: Weakley's domination-number equality conjecture for orders congruent to 1 modulo 4
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{Q}(n)$ be the $n$-Queens' graph, and let $\gamma(\mathcal{Q}(n))$ denote its domination number. For $k \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{0\}$, consider the order $n=4k+1$. **Weakley's conjecture.** For all $k \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{0\}$,

$$
2k+1=\gamma(\mathcal{Q}(4k+1)).
$$

The conjecture asserts that the known lower bound is sharp for every nonnegative integer $k$; it is verified for $k \in \{1,\dots,32\}$, while the general case remains open.

record.title: The sublinear conjugacy-class conjecture for primitive wreath-product subgroups
record.statement:
Let $A$ be an almost simple primitive group on $m$ points appearing in the paper's table of final exceptions, and assume that $k(A)<m$. For each primitive subgroup $G\leqslant A\wr S_r$ acting on $n=m^r$ points, write $k(G)$ for the number of conjugacy classes of $G$. **Sublinear conjugacy-class conjecture.** For every such $G$,

$$
k(G)=o(m^r)\qquad\text{as }r\rightarrow\infty.
$$

The conjecture seeks an improvement over the general bound $k(G)<n^{1.31}$ in the cited theorem. Earlier estimates give the desired conclusion in some cases, but not all, so the assertion is presented as an open conjecture.

record.title: Picard number conjecture for non-symmetric Kähler–Einstein toric log del Pezzo surfaces
record.statement:
Let $S$ be a **Kähler–Einstein toric log del Pezzo surface** that is not symmetric, meaning its corresponding Fano polygon is not symmetric.

**Picard number conjecture.** Then $S$ has Picard number one.

The conjecture concerns the observed structure of non-symmetric Kähler–Einstein Fano polygons. The source reports verification of the related observation for all known examples up to index $17$, but does not establish the assertion in general.

record.title: The $9_{35}$ divisibility conjecture for HOMFLY $F$-factors
record.statement:
Let $9_{35}$ be the pretzel knot under consideration. For each positive integer $i$, let $F_i$ be its $i$th $F$-factor and define

$$
F_i'=A^2q^{2i}F_i.
$$

**The $9_{35}$ divisibility conjecture.** For positive integers $i>1$,

$$
(1+A^2q^{2(i-1)})\mid F_i+F'_{i-1}.
$$

This divisibility has been verified in the paper for $2\leq i\leq 7$ and is proposed as a property of the $F$-factors for arbitrary positive $i$.
record.source_name: William Qin, “HOMFLY Polynomials of Pretzel Knots”, arXiv:2101.00695 (2021).

record.title: The $9_{46}$ odd-index transformed $F$-factor conjecture
record.statement:
Let $9_{46}$ be the pretzel knot $(3,3,-3)$, and let $F_i$ denote its $i$th $F$-factor. Define $F_i^*$ by applying the transformation $A\mapsto Aq^2$ to $F_i$ and then multiplying by $A^2/q^4$; equivalently,

$$
F_i^*=\frac{A^2}{q^4}F_i(Aq^2,q).
$$

For odd positive integers $i>1$, the quotient $F_i/(1+A^2q^{2(i-1)})$ is therefore defined by the preceding divisibility conjecture.

**The $9_{46}$ transformed-factor conjecture.**

$$
q^2(q^{2(i-1)}-1)\mid \frac{F_i}{1+A^2q^{2(i-1)}}-F^*_{i-1}.
$$

This has been verified in the paper for odd integers $3\leq i\leq 7$ and is proposed as a general pattern that may help derive arbitrary $F$-factor formulas.

record.title: Dimension greater than one for the attractors of a self-affine IFS
record.statement:
Let $0 < \lambda < \mu < 1$ with $\lambda + \mu > 1$, and define

$$
T_0(x,y)=(\lambda x,\mu y),\qquad T_1(x,y)=(\mu x+1-\mu,\lambda y+1-\lambda).
$$

Let $A_{\lambda,\mu}$ be the attractor of the iterated function system $\{T_0,T_1\}$.

**Dimension conjecture.** For all $0 < \lambda < \mu < 1$ with $\lambda + \mu > 1$, the set $A_{\lambda,\mu}$ has dimension strictly greater than $1$.

The paper proves the claim for a range of parameters occupying 91.8% of the parameter space, while the range satisfying both this result and the top-boundary theorem occupies 91.3%. The authors note that their technique may not extend arbitrarily close to all parameters, so the assertion remains open.
record.source_name: Kevin G. Hare and Nikita Sidorov, “On a family of Self-Affine IFS whose attractors have a non-fractal top”, arXiv:2101.01798 (2021).

record.title: Hausdorff-dimension conjecture for exceptional triples in the directed landscape
record.statement:
Let $X$ be the set of triples $(y,s,t)$ with $y\in\mathbb{R}$ and $s<t$. Equip $X$ with the metric

$$
d((y_1,s_1,t_1),(y_2,s_2,t_2))=|t_1-t_2|+|s_1-s_2|+|y_1-y_2|^{3/2}.
$$

For $k\geq2$, let $E_k$ be the subset of triples with $|s-t|\geq1$ for which there are at least $k$ maximizers $x_1,\ldots,x_k$ of $x\mapsto\mathcal{L}(y,s;x,t)$ satisfying $|x_i-x_j|\geq1$ for all $1\leq i<j\leq k$. **Directed-landscape exceptional-set dimension conjecture.** Almost surely,

$$
\dim_H(E_k)=\max\{3-k/3,0\},
$$

and $E_{10}$ is empty. The metric is adapted to KPZ space-time scaling, making the Hausdorff-dimension assertion a natural space-time analogue of exceptional-time dimension questions; these claims are presented as conjectural in the paper.
record.source_name: Ivan Corwin, Alan Hammond, Milind Hegde and Konstantin Matetski, “Exceptional times when the KPZ fixed point violates Johansson's conjecture on maximizer uniqueness”, arXiv:2101.04205 (2022).

record.title: Borel extra-dimension-six ideals are tripod ideals
record.statement:
A monomial ideal of $\Bbbk[X_1,X_2,X_3]$ is a **tripod ideal** if it has minimal generators of the form

$$
X_1^{a},X_1^{b}X_2^{c},X_1^{d}X_3^{e},X_2^{f},X_2^{g}X_3^{h},X_3^{i}.
$$

A Borel ideal is a monomial ideal fixed in the relevant lexicographic order. **Tripod-ideal conjecture.** Every Borel ideal of $\Bbbk[X_1,X_2,X_3]$ with extra dimension $6$ is a tripod ideal.

The claim is supported in the paper by checking monomial ideals of colength at most $25$. Its validity for all colengths remains open.

record.title: The existence conjecture for 12-regular circulant nut graphs
record.statement: A **circulant nut graph** $C(n,S)$ is a circulant graph on $n$ vertices whose adjacency matrix has nullity one and whose nullvector has no zero entries; here $S=\{a_1,a_2,\dots,a_6\}$ specifies the six positive circulant steps, giving degree $12$. **The 12-regular circulant nut graph conjecture.** For every even $n$, $n\ge 16$, there exists a circulant nut graph $C(n,\{a_1,a_2,\dots,a_6\})$ of degree $12$. The conjecture extends the explicitly constructed examples for several even orders between $16$ and $38$ and asks for such a graph at every even order at least $16$.

record.title: Square DLA exponent conjecture
record.statement:
Let ${\sf TDLA}_0(n,[0,+\infty)^2)$ be the square DLA tree with $n$ vertices, rooted at the corner ${\bf c}$, and let ${\bf v}$ be a uniformly sampled vertex of the tree. Write $w(t_n)$ for its Euclidean width and $d_{t_n}({\bf c},{\bf v})$ for the graph distance from the root corner to ${\bf v}$. **The square DLA exponent conjecture.** Both

$$
\frac{w(t_n)}{n^\alpha}\qquad\text{and}\qquad\frac{d_{t_n}({\bf c},{\bf v})}{n^\beta}
$$

converge in distribution when $\alpha=\beta$, for some $\alpha\in[0.55,0.61]$. The claim is an empirically motivated prediction for the common geometric and intrinsic scaling exponent of square DLA; the source reports simulations and no proof or resolution.

record.title: Square-root width exponent conjecture for uniform spanning trees
record.statement:
Let $t_n$ be a uniformly sampled tree of size approximately $n$ in the square-torus uniform spanning-tree model, and let $w(t_n)$ be its Euclidean width. **The UST width exponent conjecture.** The rescaled width

$$
\frac{w(t_n)}{n^\alpha}
$$

converges in distribution for some $\alpha\in[0.50,0.55]$. This is an empirical prediction based on simulations of conditioned uniform spanning-tree components; the source gives no proof or resolution.

record.title: Matsumoto–Ohno interpolation conjecture for face hypergraphs of planar triangulations
record.statement:
Let $H$ be a $3$-uniform face hypergraph obtained from a planar triangulation. A coloring of $H$ is **complete** if every pair of colors occurs together in some hyperedge; write $\chi(H)$ for the chromatic number and $\psi(H)$ for the achromatic number of $H$.

**Matsumoto–Ohno conjecture.** If $H$ is $3$-colorable, then it admits a complete $t$-coloring for every integer $t$ satisfying

$$
\chi(H) \le t \le \psi(H).
$$

The conjecture proposes the interpolation property for complete colorings in this special family of face hypergraphs. The source states that it is disproved in the paper by a particular hypergraph of order $12$.
record.source_name: Nastaran Haghparast, Morteza Hasanvand and Yumiko Ohno, “The existence of uniform hypergraphs for which interpolation property of complete coloring fails”, arXiv:2103.02034 (2021).

record.title: Martínez–Roldán–Rubin transversal conjecture for pairwise intersecting convex sets
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite family of convex sets in $\mathbb{R}^3$, with every two elements of $\mathcal{F}$ intersecting. A **line transversal** to a subfamily is a line intersecting every member of that subfamily. **Martínez–Roldán–Rubin's transversal conjecture.** There is a constant $\alpha>0$ such that $\mathcal{F}$ contains a subfamily $\mathcal{F}^*$ with

$$
|\mathcal{F}^*|\geqslant \alpha|\mathcal{F}|
$$

that has a line transversal. The conjecture asks for a positive-density line-transversal subfamily in every finite pairwise intersecting family of convex sets in three-dimensional space. The paper proves this conjecture for cylinders, with $\alpha=1/28$; the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Imre Barany, “Pairwise intersecting convex sets and cylinders in ^3”, arXiv:2104.02148 (2021).

record.title: The nonchalant-word infinitude conjecture
record.statement:
Fix an ordered alphabet $\mathbb A_n=\{\mathtt{1,2,\dots,n}\}$. Define nonchalant words recursively by $N_1=\mathtt 1$ and $N_{i+1}=N_i'xN_i”$, where this is a square-free extension of $N_i$, $N_i”$ is the shortest possible suffix of $N_i$, and $x\in\mathbb A_n$ is the earliest possible letter.

**Nonchalant-word infinitude conjecture.** The sequence of nonchalant words over $\mathbb A_n$ is infinite for every $n\geqslant 3$.

The conjecture asserts that the greedy construction never stops. Computer experiments support it, including a ternary nonchalant word of length $10000$, but the general claim remains open.

record.title: The extremal PageRank distance conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be any unweighted directed graph, possibly with loops and bidirected arcs, and let $\alpha_1$ and $\alpha_2$ be two jumping constants. For each jumping constant, write $\pi_{\alpha_i}$ for the corresponding PageRank vector. **Extremal PageRank distance conjecture.** For every such graph and every pair $\alpha_1,\alpha_2$, 

$$
\\|\pi_{\alpha_1}-\pi_{\alpha_2}\\| < \sqrt{\frac{67}{50}}.
$$

The paper's main theorem constructs unweighted directed graphs whose PageRank distance approaches $\sqrt{67/50}$ from below, so this conjecture asserts that the limiting value is the best possible universal bound. Its status is not resolved by the supplied text.
record.source_name: Joseph Farnan and Franklin H. J. Kenter, “A Tale of Two Limits: An Extremal Pagerank Problem”, arXiv:2104.07727 (2021).

record.title: The positive-integer edge-Kempe class conjecture for bipartite cubic graphs
record.statement:
For a cubic graph, consider its 3-edge-colorings and the equivalence relation generated by edge-Kempe switches. The resulting equivalence classes are called **edge-Kempe equivalence classes**. A bipartite cubic graph is a cubic graph whose vertex set has a bipartition such that every edge joins the two parts.

**Positive-integer edge-Kempe class conjecture.** For any positive integer $m$, there is a bipartite cubic graph with exactly $m$ edge-Kempe equivalence classes.

The paper reports that all positive integers up to $106$ occur in its computations, motivating this existence conjecture. It remains open for arbitrary positive integers.
record.source_name: Jan Goedgebeur and Patric R. J. Östergård, “Switching 3-edge-colorings of cubic graphs”, arXiv:2105.01363 (2021).
